claims.text: Incomplete recovery of cold-worked HfNbTaTiZr produces persistent local lattice-parameter gradients.
Persistent local lattice-parameter gradients generate internal thermal stresses during heating.
These internal thermal stresses govern the anomalous high-temperature stress–strain and thermoelastic responses of HfNbTaTiZr.
A 50% cold-rolling reduction induces a heterogeneous microstructure in equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Full homogenization annealing eliminates lattice-parameter gradients in cold-rolled HfNbTaTiZr.
A short anneal at 600–800 °C produces only partial recovery and preserves heterogeneous strain fields.
Comparing fully homogenized and partially recovered specimens is intended to isolate the effect of retained microstructural heterogeneity.
Incomplete recovery leaves spatial variations in lattice parameters and residual dislocation networks.
The retained heterogeneity produces a thermal-expansion mismatch between grain interiors and grain boundaries.
Regions with different lattice parameters expand at different rates during heating.
Differential thermal expansion generates internal thermal stresses.
The generated internal thermal stresses modulate dislocation motion and thereby affect creep.
The generated internal thermal stresses alter the temperature dependence of elastic moduli.
Partially recovered specimens will have higher apparent yield strength at 1250 °C than fully homogenized specimens.
Partially recovered specimens will have greater creep resistance at 1250 °C than fully homogenized specimens.
Partially recovered specimens will deviate from the fully homogenized baseline modulus–temperature trend between 293 and 1100 K.
Fully homogenized specimens have minimal lattice-parameter gradients and insignificant internal thermal stresses.
Annealing-induced changes in grain-boundary chemistry or dislocation density may contribute to the measured responses independently of thermal-expansion mismatch.
A lack of consistent, statistically significant mechanical or thermoelastic differences despite substantial residual lattice-parameter gradients would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
